items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 27 at 4:20AM AKDT until October 28 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 2 to 4 feet above the normal
high tide line. Water levels are expected to peak Tuesday
evening.

* WHERE...Baldwin Peninsula and Northern Seward Peninsula Coast.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Localized beach erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Wind gusts will peak around 45 to 55 mph
out of the south/southeast. Water levels remain slightly above
normal, but slowly lower through the end of the week after
Tuesday.
items.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

items.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued October 27 at 4:00AM AKDT until October 29 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 6 and
18 inches. Winds gusting as high as 35 mph.

* WHERE...Red Dog Mine and the South Slopes of the Western Brooks
Range.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 4 PM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow
could significantly reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Mostly rain is expected below 800 feet. The
heaviest precipitation is expected Tuesday and Wednesday. Some rain

items.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 27 at 3:39AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
ESFAFG

Areas of concern are between Nome and Council, particularity streams
and rivers draining the south aspects of the high elevation terrain
of the Seward Peninsula.

Rivers and streams in the Nome and Council area are already high
following rainfall over the weekend. 1-3 more inches of precipitation
are expected by the end of the week which will keep water levels
high.

No flooding is expected at this time, however residents living near
local rivers and streams should be vigilant of the pot
items.areas: Southern Seward Peninsula Coast; Interior Seward Peninsula

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 27 at 3:36AM AKDT until October 29 at 7:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...South winds 30 to 45 mph with gusts up to 65 mph expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp and Windy Pass.

* WHEN...From 7 AM Wednesday to 7 AM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.
items.areas: Northern Denali Borough; Eastern Alaska Range North of Trims Camp
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

items.headline: High Wind Warning issued October 27 at 3:35AM AKDT until October 27 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...South winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts up to 60 mph expected.

* WHERE...Bering Strait Coast, Diomede, and St Lawrence Island.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...High winds may move loose debris, damage property and
cause power outages. Travel could be difficult.
items.areas: Shishmaref; Bering Strait Coast; St Lawrence Island
items.instruction:
People are urged to secure loose objects that could be blown around
or damaged by the wind.

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 27 at 2:26AM AKDT until October 28 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:

* WHEN...From 10 PM this evening to 10 AM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and a few

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Southeast winds will become strong and gusty

items.areas: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
